name: Opposites
blurb: Find the word that means the opposite.
childIntro: Read the word. Then find the answer that means the opposite of it.
howItWorks: The child reads a word and picks its opposite from five choices. It appears at OLSAT levels D through G, so grade 3 and up. The distractors are built to be near misses: usually several of them are synonyms of the stem word rather than opposites.
parentTip: The classic hard version gives four synonyms and one true antonym. If your child picks a word that means the same thing, they have understood the word but not the question. Ask them first: am I looking for same or opposite? Saying it out loud fixes most of these errors.

questions.explanation: Brave means not afraid, so its opposite is afraid. Bold, heroic and daring all mean roughly the same as brave.
questions.strategy: Cross off every word that means the SAME as the first word. They are all traps.

questions.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern. Old and historic mean the same as ancient.
questions.strategy: Ancient and modern. Old and new. Learn opposite pairs together.

questions.explanation: Shallow describes how far down something goes, so its opposite is deep. Wide and narrow are about how far across, which is a different measurement.
questions.strategy: Check which direction the word measures: down, across or along.

questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give, so its opposite is selfish. Kind, giving and friendly all point the same way as generous. Wealthy is about money, not about sharing.
questions.strategy: One word will be about a different idea altogether. That one is not the answer either.

questions.explanation: Temporary means lasting only a short time, so its opposite is permanent, which means lasting for ever. Brief, short and quick all mean the same as temporary.
questions.strategy: Four synonyms and one antonym is the hardest build. Find the odd one out and check it really is the opposite.

questions.explanation: Expand means to get bigger, so its opposite is shrink. Grow, stretch, widen and swell all mean to get bigger.
questions.strategy: Verbs have opposites too. Ask which way the action goes.

questions.explanation: Scarce means there is very little of it, so its opposite is plentiful. Rare means the same as scarce. Valuable is often true of scarce things but it is not the opposite.
questions.strategy: Something that often goes WITH a word is not its opposite.

questions.explanation: Arrive means to get to a place, so its opposite is depart, which means to leave. Reach, enter and land all mean much the same as arrive.
questions.strategy: Coming and going. Many opposites are simply a change of direction.

questions.explanation: Transparent means you can see through it, so its opposite is opaque, which means you cannot. Clear and glassy mean the same as transparent. Fragile is about breaking, a different idea.
questions.strategy: If you do not know a word, still cross off the ones that mean the same as the first word.

questions.explanation: Conceal means to hide something, so its opposite is reveal, which means to show it. Hide, cover and bury all mean the same as conceal.
questions.strategy: Con-ceal and re-veal. Some opposite pairs even rhyme, which makes them easier to remember.

questions.explanation: Heavy means it weighs a lot, so its opposite is light. Large is about size, not weight, and a small thing can still be heavy.
questions.strategy: Check what the word measures: weight, size, length or amount.

questions.explanation: Early means before the expected time, so its opposite is late. Soon and quick are about speed, not about being before or after.
questions.strategy: Time words come in pairs. Early and late, before and after.

questions.explanation: Gather means to bring things together, so its opposite is scatter, which spreads them apart. Collect and pile both mean the same as gather.
questions.strategy: Cross off every word that means the SAME as the first word.

questions.explanation: Rough means the surface is not even, so its opposite is smooth. Bumpy, coarse and uneven all mean the same as rough.
questions.strategy: Four words meaning the same and one meaning the opposite is a common trap.

questions.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern. Aged, antique and historic are all ways of saying old.
questions.strategy: If a word feels like a fancier version of the first word, it is not the opposite.

questions.explanation: Shrink means to get smaller, so its opposite is expand, which means to get bigger. Reduce and narrow both mean to get smaller.
questions.strategy: Verbs have direction. Ask which way the action goes: bigger or smaller.

questions.explanation: Accept means to say yes to something, so its opposite is refuse. Receive, take and agree all point the same way as accept.
questions.strategy: Saying yes and saying no. Many opposite pairs are just that.

questions.explanation: Artificial means made by people rather than grown, so its opposite is natural. Fake, man-made and copied all mean the same as artificial.
questions.strategy: A long word still has a simple opposite. Say what it means in your own words first.

questions.explanation: Scatter means to spread things apart, so its opposite is collect, which brings them together. Spread, toss and sprinkle all mean the same as scatter.
questions.strategy: This is the reverse of an earlier question. Opposite pairs work in both directions.

questions.explanation: Permanent means it lasts for ever, so its opposite is temporary, which lasts only a short time. Lasting, fixed and steady all mean the same as permanent.
questions.strategy: Learn opposite pairs together: permanent and temporary, always and never.

questions.explanation: Cautious means being very careful, so its opposite is reckless, which means not careful at all. Careful, wary and alert all mean the same as cautious. Nervous is a feeling, not a way of acting.
questions.strategy: One distractor is usually about a different idea entirely. That one is not the answer either.

questions.explanation: Abundant means there is a great deal of it, so its opposite is scarce, which means there is very little. Plentiful, ample and rich all mean the same as abundant.
questions.strategy: When four words agree with each other, the fifth is your answer.

questions.explanation: Ascend means to go up, so its opposite is descend, which means to go down. Climb, rise, lift and soar all go upwards.
questions.strategy: The beginnings of words help. Ascend goes up, descend goes down.

questions.explanation: Fragile means it breaks easily, so its opposite is sturdy, which means strong and hard to break. Delicate, brittle and weak all mean the same as fragile.
questions.strategy: Cross off the synonyms first. Whatever is left is usually the answer.

questions.explanation: Conceal means to hide something, so its opposite is reveal, which means to show it. Hide, bury, cover and mask all mean the same as conceal.
questions.strategy: Con-ceal and re-veal even rhyme, which makes the pair easy to remember.

questions.explanation: Humble means not boastful, so its opposite is arrogant, which means very boastful. Modest means the same as humble. Quiet and shy describe how loud or confident a person is, which is a different idea.
questions.strategy: Check that the word is about the same idea, not just about people in general.

questions.explanation: Depart means to go away from a place, so its opposite is arrive, which means to reach it. Leave, exit and withdraw all mean the same as depart.
questions.strategy: Coming and going. Many opposites are simply a change of direction.

questions.explanation: Opaque means you cannot see through it, so its opposite is transparent, which means you can. Cloudy and murky both mean the same as opaque.
questions.strategy: Even for an unfamiliar word, crossing off the synonyms narrows it down fast.

questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give freely, so its opposite is stingy, which means unwilling to give. Giving, kind and charitable all mean the same as generous. Wealthy is about money, not about sharing it.
questions.strategy: Rich and generous are different ideas. Do not mix them up.

questions.explanation: Victory means winning, so its opposite is defeat, which means losing. Triumph, success and win all mean the same as victory. A prize is what you get for one.
questions.strategy: The result of a thing is not its opposite.

questions.explanation: Complex means made of many parts, so its opposite is simple. Complicated and intricate mean the same as complex. Difficult is close but means hard to do, which is not quite the same as having many parts.
questions.strategy: When two answers seem possible, pick the one that matches the exact meaning.

questions.explanation: Diligent means working hard and carefully, so its opposite is lazy. Hardworking, careful and thorough all mean the same as diligent. Busy is close but describes having a lot to do, not working hard at it.
questions.strategy: Busy and hardworking are not the same. Read the shade of meaning.

questions.explanation: Amplify means to make a sound louder, so its opposite is muffle, which makes it quieter. Increase, boost, magnify and strengthen all mean to make something greater.
questions.strategy: Match the exact thing being changed. Here it is loudness, not size.

questions.explanation: Optional means you may choose whether to do it, so its opposite is required, which means you must. Voluntary and chosen both mean the same as optional.
questions.strategy: Must and may. Rules words come in that pair.
